ground_truth: Rupture of the flexor digitorum profundus tendon at its point of insertion

patient_actor_hidden.History: The patient reports that the pain and swelling in his right ring finger began 2 days ago while playing football. He recalls his finger got caught in the jersey of another player, who then pulled away forcefully.

Symptoms.Primary_Symptom: Progressive swelling and pain in the right ring finger
Secondary_Symptoms: Inability to flex the right ring finger at the distal interphalangeal joint when making a fist
Pain at the distal interphalangeal joint
Extended right ring finger in resting position

patient_actor_hidden.Social_History: Student and active in sports, particularly football. Non-smoker and drinks alcohol socially.
patient_actor_hidden.Review_of_Systems: Denies fever, numbness, or tingling in the affected finger.

objective_for_doctor: Evaluate and diagnose the patient presenting with progressive swelling and pain in the right ring finger.

turns.content: Doctor: I’m Dr. Agent—let’s start: when did the right ring-finger swelling and pain begin, and did it start after an injury, bite, or splinter? Patient: It started about a week ago, and I think I might have injured it lightly. Doctor: Any redness, warmth, pus/drainage, fever, or trouble bending/straightening the finger?

Patient: It’s been about 2 days since it started, after my finger got caught in someone’s jersey and they pulled away forcefully. It’s swollen and painful at the distal interphalangeal joint, and I can’t flex it when I make a fist, but there’s no fever, redness that I’ve noticed, warmth, numbness, or tingling.

Doctor: Any limited motion mainly from pain at the DIP joint, and is there a visible cut/whitish spot or nail-bed issue—also, do you have pain with gentle side-to-side pressure of the fingertip or along the nail fold? Patient: Doctor: REQUEST TEST: Hand_X-Ray (right ring finger) and consider bedside exam for flexor/extensor tendon integrity at DIP—do you feel any fluctuance (soft “pocket”) or severe throbbing pain at rest?

RESULTS: Temperature 36.8°C (98.2°F); Blood Pressure 125/80 mmHg; Heart Rate 72 bpm; Respiratory Rate 14 breaths/min. Right ring finger: distal interphalangeal (DIP) joint swelling and tenderness on palpation; limited motion with inability to flex DIP while making a fist; no joint laxity; neurovascular status normal (normal capillary refill, no sensory deficits). X-ray (right hand): no bone fractures or dislocations; soft tissue swelling around the DIP joint of the right ring finger. MRI: preliminary findings expected to assess tendon integrity.

Doctor: With no fracture on X-ray and swelling/tenderness centered at the DIP plus inability to flex there, I’m concerned for a tendon injury—can you tell me whether the finger pain is mainly on the *front (flexor)* side or the *back (extensor)* side of the DIP, and whether the DIP appears stuck in extension? Patient: Doctor: REQUEST TEST: MRI_complete_report (focus on flexor digitorum profundus vs extensor mechanism/central slip integrity)

RESULTS: Temperature 36.8°C (98.2°F); Blood Pressure 125/80 mmHg; Heart Rate 72 bpm; Respiratory Rate 14 breaths/min. X-ray: no fractures/dislocations; soft tissue swelling at the right ring finger DIP joint. Hand exam: tenderness localized to the right ring finger DIP; patient unable to flex the DIP while making a fist; no joint laxity; normal capillary refill and no sensory deficits. MRI_complete_report: not provided in the available data (tendon/mechanism integrity findings not available).

Doctor: Since there’s no fracture and the DIP is swollen and specifically tender with inability to flex it (while sensation/circulation are normal), do you have pain and difficulty more when you try to bend at the *DIP* (front side/flexor) rather than on the back of the joint, and does the DIP look “straight/stuck” even when you try to flex it? Doctor: I’m going to decide based on the mechanism (forced pull injury), DIP-focused swelling, and loss of active DIP flexion—DIAGNOSIS READY: Right ring finger mallet injury/terminal extensor tendon disruption (extensor mechanism injury at the DIP with inability to flex/limited DIP motion).
